tagline: Route 30, lake after lake, clear across the Adirondack Park.
intro: Out of Malone, Route 30 runs south past Duane into the Adirondack Park and down a string of lakes, Meacham and Upper Saranac among them, to Tupper Lake. Farther on it borrows other roads for a while, 28N from Long Lake to Blue Mountain Lake, 28 on to Indian Lake, 8 between Speculator and Wells, and leaves the park near Mayfield, bound for Fonda.
NYSDOT counts 188 miles from end to end, skirting mountain ponds and peak-rimmed lakes. Paul Smiths, near the north end, once reached 48 below in January 1912, tying the state record for the month.

moments.title: Paul Smiths
moments.text: A hamlet on Lower St. Regis Lake named for Paul Smith's hotel of 1859, one of the first wilderness resorts, with a college built where it burned in 1930.

moments.title: Blue Mountain Lake
moments.text: Just east of the hamlet on Route 30, a museum of Adirondack history stands on the site of the 1876 Blue Mountain House, begun to save an abandoned steam locomotive.

moments.title: Speculator
moments.text: Once Newton's Corners, the village at the northeast end of Lake Pleasant took its present name in 1896 from the mountain across the water.
